question: Why is research governance so important in midwifery studies?

options.A: To protect human participants from harm and respect their rights
options.B: To speed up the publication process in medical journals
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of conducting hospital surveys
options.D: To secure financial grants from international health bodies

explanation: Research governance is put in place primarily to safeguard the wellbeing, dignity, and rights of individuals who take part in studies. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why must midwifery research proposals go through an ethical review before data collection begins?

options.A: To ensure the researcher has enough funding to complete the fieldwork
options.B: To determine the exact journal where the final paper will be published
options.C: To verify that the study's benefits outweigh any potential risks to participants
options.D: To check if the statistical formulas used in the methodology are correct

explanation: Ethics committees evaluate study plans to ensure that what we learn will be valuable while keeping any physical or emotional risks to participants as low as possible. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h1)

question: What key detail must be stated in every research informed consent form?

options.A: Participants waive their right to confidentiality once the study is published
options.B: Participants are legally obligated to complete all study questionnaires
options.C: Participants can withdraw at any time without losing routine clinical care
options.D: Participants will receive a guaranteed cash payment for their time

explanation: Taking part in research is totally voluntary. Patients must always know they can stop whenever they want without affecting their regular hospital treatment. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h2)

question: A midwife is planning a study in a rural clinic in Northern Nigeria. What is the best approach for the consent documents?

options.A: Ask the hospital manager to sign consent on behalf of all patients
options.B: Use complex medical terminology to ensure scientific accuracy
options.C: Translate the forms into the local language understood by the community
options.D: Require verbal consent only without providing any written information

explanation: For true informed consent, participants need to fully understand what the study involves, which means translating materials into the language they speak every day. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a common reason for delays in getting ethical review approval?

options.A: Missing recruitment materials in the submitted document package
options.B: Failing to explain potential risks clearly in the consent form
options.C: Providing complete and clear translation of all questionnaires
options.D: Vague descriptions of how patient data will be kept secure

explanation: Clear and complete translations actually help move your application along faster. Vague descriptions or missing paperwork are what usually slow things down. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the main focus of an Ethics Committee when looking at a midwifery research protocol?

options.A: Ensuring the research results will be published in high-impact journals
options.B: Calculating the exact financial profit the hospital will gain from the study
options.C: Safeguarding the welfare and confidentiality of human participants
options.D: Reviewing the literary style and grammar of the research introduction

explanation: Ethics boards exist solely to protect human subjects from harm, making sure their privacy and personal rights are respected throughout the study. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h3)

question: What type of data collection tool uses a list of written questions to gather information from a large group of people?
explanation: A questionnaire is a structured set of written questions used to collect information efficiently from many respondents at once. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why should researchers avoid leading questions when writing a questionnaire?

options.A: Leading questions require advanced statistical software to analyze properly
options.B: Leading questions make the questionnaire too long for busy pregnant women
options.C: Leading questions are automatically rejected by institutional ethics boards
options.D: Leading questions can bias the respondents and distort the accuracy of data

explanation: Questions that nudge a patient toward a certain answer will give you unreliable results that do not reflect the true situation. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of pilot testing a research tool before your actual study?

options.A: To recruit participants for the main study from the pilot group
options.B: To publish the final research findings in an international journal early
options.C: To secure final financial grants from the hospital management board
options.D: To identify confusing questions and estimate completion time before the main study

explanation: Pilot testing lets you catch unclear wording, formatting issues, and time delays so you can fix them before starting the main data collection. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h5)

question: A midwife researcher just drafted a new questionnaire on antenatal clinic attendance. What is the best next step?

options.A: Conduct a pilot test with a small group of women who share similar characteristics
options.B: Destroy the draft because questionnaires cannot be changed once written
options.C: Submit the final published paper directly to a medical conference
options.D: Begin collecting data immediately from the main sample population

explanation: Testing your questions on a small, similar group helps you spot errors and make improvements before launching your big study. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h5)

question: What should a researcher do if several pilot participants misunderstand a specific survey question?

options.A: Remove all open-ended questions from the study entirely
options.B: Ignore the feedback and keep the question exactly the same
options.C: Reword or simplify the question to improve clarity
options.D: Blame the participants for lacking formal education

explanation: If people keep misunderstanding a question during a pilot test, it means the wording is unclear and needs to be revised. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h6)

question: How does refining your research tool after a pilot test help your study?

options.A: It guarantees that the study will receive immediate international funding
options.B: It improves data reliability and validity by removing confusing items
options.C: It eliminates the need to obtain ethical clearance from the board
options.D: It reduces the total number of participants needed for the study

explanation: Clearing up confusing questions ensures your tool consistently measures what it is supposed to, which makes your overall study much stronger. [learn more](BMP314_U1_T4#BMP314_U1_T4_h6)
